minutes.headline: Committee set how to review design RFQ responses: completeness check Jan 8, individual scoring, then interviews.
minutes.summary: The TCP Building Design Committee discussed how to evaluate responses to the design RFQ, which was advertised the prior week with a due date around January 7-8. It agreed on a completeness review and packet distribution on January 8, individual scoring, a later composite score, and possibly interviewing more than three firms. Members also debated proposing ideas for the vacated buildings, and the meeting was tabled to continue at the TCP tour.

what_happened.line: The committee agreed on a plan for reviewing design RFQ responses: a completeness review on January 8, then individual scoring by each member.
Members will combine their individual scores into a composite score at a later meeting, and may interview more than three firms.
The committee will ask the procurement officer to confirm that proposals are complete and to take part in interviews.
The committee will check with the procurement officer in early January on how many proposals have arrived before it fixes the review schedule.
Members discussed ideas for the vacated buildings, then tabled the meeting to continue at the TCP tour; the vote count was not audible.

why_it_matters: The scoring method and schedule set here decide how the design firm for the TCP building project is chosen, and that choice shapes a project residents will be asked to pay for.
A member raised the effect on the tax bill of maintaining two more empty buildings, a cost that depends on what happens to the vacated buildings and was not resolved.
